newsitem.title: USA: Three Coast Guard crewmen die in Pacific Ocean.
newsitem.headline: Three Coast Guard crewmen die in Pacific Ocean.

text.p: Three Coast Guard crewmen on a rescue mission died when rough seas capsized their motorized lifeboat and threw them into frigid waters Wednesday, officials said.
A fourth crew member survived the accident near the Olympic Peninsula town of La Push with minor injuries, Petty Officer Steve Carlton said.

Seaman Clinton Miniken, 22, of Snohomish, Wash., was declared dead several hours after searchers found him on a beach with no vital signs and took him to nearby Forks Community Hospital, where doctors tried to revive him.

Petty Officer David Bosley, 36, of Coronado, Calif., and Petty Officer Matthew Schlimme, 24, of Whitewater, Mo., were found floating face down in a cove of tiny James Island at the mouth of the Quillayute River near their station. Their capsized 44-foot lifeboat was found nearby.
Seaman Benjamin Wingo, 19, of Bremerton, Wash., was reported in satisfactory condition with scrapes and a broken nose. A cliff rescue team used rappelling gear to rescue him from a crevice.

The accident occurred shortly after two boats and a helicopter were sent out at 12:30 a.m. PST (3:30 a.m. EST) in response to a distress call from two people in a sailboat taking on water in seas of up to 25 feet and winds of up to 45 knots.

As the rescue boats entered the Pacific Ocean at the mouth of the Quillayute River they lost sight of each other and no further radio transmissions were heard from one of them. Crew members on the other vessel saw one emergency flare and then four more in quick succession.
Several more helicopters were dispatched to the area but, despite infrared radar, "with the heavy seas, rain and wind it was very hard to locate anything," LaGuardia said."
Chief Petty Officer Carolyn Cihelka said the boat apparently capsized as it was crossing the area where the river meets the ocean and creates particularly dangerous surf.

"Just about all the rivers along the west coast of Oregon and Washington have this condition, and every one is a very hazardous crossing every time you go out there," she said. "Of course, when you have conditions like you did today it just exacerbates it."

The foundering sailboat was located five miles south of James Island and the couple, identified as U.S. Navy Lt. Kenneth Schlag and his wife, were rescued by helicopter shortly before their vessel was smashed on the rocks.

They were taken to the Forks hospital where they were treated for hypothermia. Schlag and his wife, whose name was not immediately available, had been relocating the pleasure boat Gale Runner from California to his new station in Bremerton, a Coast Guard spokesman said.
Minniken was found just before 4 a.m. PST but the other crew members were not reached until several hours later.

All crew members aboard both boats were following standard procedure that calls for them to wear crash helmets and survival suits designed to keep them alive for at least two hours in waters currently about 50 degrees Fahrenheit.
It was the worst loss of life in a single incident for the Coast Guard since a 1994 helicopter crash in California killed all four crew members aboard.
